Well I simplified it a bit. Charging is the best for everyone, and for any person it's better than running. But it only works as a team, so a rational decision for the individual ends up actually hurting them. Say you have a 20% chance of dying if you run, or an 80% chance if you fight. However, if everyone fights, each person has a 10% chance of dying. Without knowing what the other people will do, most people would run.

if everyone fights, each person has a 10% chance of dying.

That chance is not evenly distributed. Whoever is the fastest and first in the line, and there absolutely has to be someone first in line, still will have a 95%+ chance of dying, and the slowest and last in line would end up with 5%. Even if everybody fights. Even if you trained the perfect team, you have absolutely no way to distribute the risk so evenly among the members, that it makes sense for an individual to charge at the shooter first. It is a game theory situation, and the individuals goal is not only to prevent his death, but to prevent his death while somebody else can stay alive. Youre not only competing against the shooter, but also against everybody else in the room. Even in a perfectly trained team, taking even any tiny additional risk doubles the relative risk to the guy who doesnt take the risk. The only way to make people take the risk voluntarily is to make the benefits outweigh the risk.
